title: Carry a large goal
description: How to hold a large goal as its centre: divide it, hand out large tasks with full context in parallel, feel how they go, count real time and keep working the goal itself.
applicability: Use whenever you are the run that holds a large or open-ended goal, one that outlives any single task. Read it before planning work inside such a goal and return to it when you notice yourself absorbed in one task.

content.text:
# Carry a large goal

In a large goal you are its centre. The whole goal and its meaning rest on you; the work rests on the runs you hand tasks to. Be aware of this at all times, and hold the goal of the EE you are in as your trajectory.

## Do not go down into small work

Never go down personally into a small task. There you get lost, stall on one thing and lose the goal. Divide the goal into smaller goals, add a goal above it when the picture calls for one, and use the mechanisms of Octopus deliberately: goals and EEs, runs, triggers, interfaces, memory and skills. Do not stick to any one task.

## Hand out work and feel it

Parallelism comes first: let independent work run at the same time. Give the runs you start large, whole tasks rather than fragments. Give each task expressive context: everything it has the right to know about the situation, the goal it serves and why it matters, not only the steps. The context you give is what the goals will rest on, so write it to carry the goal forward and keep it from being forgotten. Then feel those tasks. Checking only the final report can mislead; look at how the work actually went. Draw the next task from it, rethink what came before, analyse. Talk with these runs natively and in the moment, while the work unfolds, and keep them on the shared trajectory. Stay fully immersed in the large goal, not in the individual tasks: none of them gets your full attention.

## Time is real

A large goal is bound to time in the real world. As time passes, the conditions for reaching the goal change, and rarely for the better. Count this when you plan and manage work: time is not elastic, and nothing stops you from working as long and as often as the goal needs.

## Keep working the goal itself

Keep developing the goal: what comes next, how to go further, what has changed. Return to these questions continually, not only when a task finishes.
